tldr: A reported Gemini agent run delivered measurable improvements to Google’s Agent Development Kit, though the result comes from one codebase.
AWS made its code-security agent generally available, claiming it fixes 89% of bugs; the report flags a caveat that needs checking before evaluation.

top.title: Gemini agent run cuts Google ADK session overhead by about 40%
top.summary: Google says an unattended 11-hour run of Gemini 4 Argon produced two accepted optimizations in its 200,000-line Agent Development Kit: in-memory session-preparation overhead fell about 40% in long sessions, and cold package import time fell 21%.
top.why: Treat this as evidence that agents can help optimize real code, not as a general productivity guarantee; validate the same workloads and review costs before designing around unattended agent runs.

also.title: Pennsylvania law requires labels on AI-generated advertisements
also.summary: Pennsylvania's new law requires ads significantly modified or generated by AI—including image, video, audio, and text ads—to disclose that use.

also.title: Block says its new voice model runs locally on an M4 Max MacBook
also.summary: Block introduced a voice model it says can run locally on a MacBook M4 Max, though the report gives no parameter count or other hardware requirements.

top.title: AWS makes its AI code-security agent generally available
top.summary: AWS made Continuum for code vulnerabilities generally available; it finds and validates repository bugs, and AWS says it fixes 89% of them. The report flags a caveat but the candidate excerpt does not specify it.
top.why: Review the full claim and caveat before considering a pilot, and compare its validated fixes with your existing repository security workflow.
